newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 12.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Parliament yesterday saw the first substantial discussion of the government's plans to revise the Constitution. Among the 70 provisions to be changed - of a total 120 - are the number of votes need to elect a president and for the presidential election to be separated from a recourse to general elections if a poll for president falls short.

--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou and environmental organisation Greenpeace will hold a joint news conference aboard the Greenpeace vessel 'Syrios' today on the 4.7 billion drachma investment by US firm IWEKO in alternative energy projects in Crete.
--New York will host talks between Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash between July 9-13.

--Parliament yesterday ratified the Schengen treaty despite a substantial number of absent MPs and two policemen abandoning their duties and throwing in their lot with the faithful demonstrating outside the Parliament building.
--Some 67 percent of Greeks support the need for convergence, according to a recent MRB poll.
--The Greek investing public went into a buying frenzy yesterday for Greek telecoms organisation OTE shares with demand already estimated to have covered the shares offered.

--The US government has reiterated its reward of two million dollars for information that will help the Greek authorities arrest members of the November 17 terrorist group, responsible for a number of deaths - including US citizens - since 1974.
--Former prime minister Constantine Mitsotakis reveals that he is ready to run for president of the republic if the Constitution is changed to allow for direct elections.

--Some 84 percent of Greeks distrust politicians, believing them to be corrupt. The level of distrust comes second only to Latin American and Far East scepticism. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
